title: The Year Sugriva Waited at the Cave
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

captions.instagram:
Vali chased the demon Mayavi into a cave and made Sugriva swear to wait at its mouth. A full year passed (Valmiki Ramayana 4.9.15). Then blood flowed out, Sugriva sealed the cave with a rock and was made king (4.9.19-20). Vali's side: he called "Sugriva!" again and again and had to kick the rock open (4.10.17-19). One rock, two stories. Full 14-min video on our YouTube.

Whose side of the story do you believe: Sugriva's or Vali's?

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Critical Edition, Kishkindha Kanda 4.5, 4.9-4.25; Ramcharitmanas, Kishkindha Kand (dohas 7-11)

Verses:
• One night, a demon named Mayavi came roaring to the gate of Kishkindha. Vali rushed out to kill him, and Sugriva went with him. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.9.4-4.9.8
• The demon ran into a great cave. Vali made Sugriva swear by his feet: wait here, at the mouth. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.9.11-4.9.14
• And Sugriva waited. A whole year. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.9.15
• Then foaming red blood flowed out of the cave. He heard demons roaring, and what sounded like his elder brother's cry. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.9.17-4.9.18
• Sugriva believed his brother was dead. He sealed the cave with a mountain-sized rock and came back. The ministers made him king. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.9.19-4.9.20
• And then the brother everyone thought was dead walked back into Kishkindha. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.9.21
• Sugriva, with folded hands, gave the kingdom back: "It was only held in trust. You alone are king." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.10.3-4.10.5
• "I called again and again, 'Sugriva! Sugriva!' No answer came. I kicked that rock until it broke." — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.10.17-4.10.19
• To Vali, it was betrayal. Sugriva says Vali drove him out with a single garment, and took his wife Ruma. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.10.20-4.10.22
• One rock. Two brothers. Two stories. — Valmiki Ramayana CE 4.9.19; 4.10.17

claims.claim: One night, a demon named Mayavi came roaring to the gate of Kishkindha. Vali rushed out to kill him, and Sugriva went with him.
The demon ran into a great cave. Vali made Sugriva swear by his feet: wait here, at the mouth.
And Sugriva waited. A whole year.
Then foaming red blood flowed out of the cave. He heard demons roaring, and what sounded like his elder brother's cry.
Sugriva believed his brother was dead. He sealed the cave with a mountain-sized rock and came back. The ministers made him king.
And then the brother everyone thought was dead walked back into Kishkindha.
Sugriva, with folded hands, gave the kingdom back: "It was only held in trust. You alone are king."
"I called again and again, 'Sugriva! Sugriva!' No answer came. I kicked that rock until it broke."
To Vali, it was betrayal. Sugriva says Vali drove him out with a single garment, and took his wife Ruma.
One rock. Two brothers. Two stories.

verify_note: Every line cites CE Kishkindha; character lines are close Hindi renderings of the cited verses. Vali's line 'what merit...' is 4.17.13; Rama's hunting answer is 4.18.34-36.
